metrics.label: Key insights 01–07

value.title: The dataset-wide observation mean is 11.95 per 100,000.
value.detail: The mean across 2,843 observed country-year records is 11.95; the median is 10.64.
value.caveat: This weights each reported record equally, not each country equally, and coverage varies by year.

value.title: The highest simple yearly mean is in 1982 (14.76).
value.detail: There are 52 entities reporting in the peak year.
value.caveat: The number and composition of reporting entities change over time; the fixed eight-entity panel peaks in 1998 (12.21).

value.title: Lithuania has the highest eligible country mean (35.13).
value.detail: The ranking requires at least 10 observations; Lithuania has 23.
value.caveat: Without that rule, the raw top three are Lithuania (35.1; n=23), Guyana (30.8; n=3), Russia (30.8; n=24); short series such as Guyana (3) are less comparable.

value.title: Reporting coverage ranges from 10 entities in 1950 to 191 in 2004 and 2005.
value.detail: The reporting count varies sharply in nearby years, including 62 in 2001, 190 in 2002, 55 in 2003, and 191 in 2004.
value.caveat: A change in the yearly average can reflect changing coverage as well as changing observed rates.

value.title: Only 8 entities report in every year from 1950 through 2005.
value.detail: Their average across annual panel means is 10.67, versus 11.95 across all records.
value.caveat: This fixed panel is a small, selected group and is not representative of the full world population.

value.title: Year-over-year anomaly rules flag 122 changes by |z| > 2 and 235 by the 1.5×IQR rule.
value.detail: There are 2,457 consecutive-year country changes; 122 are flagged by both methods.
value.caveat: Flags identify unusual observed changes, not data errors or explanations; missing intervening years are not treated as annual changes.

value.title: 82 observed rates exceed the distribution's Tukey IQR fences.
value.detail: The maximum is 44.35 for Lithuania in 1996; no negative or zero rates occur.
value.caveat: Extreme values are retained because a statistical outlier alone is not evidence of an invalid record.

B1.rule: Favourable when Spearman rho >= 0.80 and n >= 30; Mixed when rho >= 0.50 and n >= 30; otherwise Not Favourable.

B2.label: Favourable
B2.rule: Favourable when Spearman rho >= 0.80 and n >= 30; Mixed when rho >= 0.50 and n >= 30; otherwise Not Favourable.
B2.reason: Spearman rho = 0.94 with n = 67: country rankings are stable enough for country-level comparison across these fixed windows.

B3.label: Mixed
B3.rule: Mixed when the full-sample |r| < 0.30 and the >=10-year subset |r| < 0.30; Not Favourable when both |r| values are >= 0.50; otherwise Mixed.
B3.reason: The full-sample association is weak (r = 0.23) and it is absent among the 68 countries with at least 10 years (r = -0.05).

B4.label: Not Favourable
B4.rule: Not Favourable when Pearson r >= 0.50 and n >= 30; Mixed for 0.30-0.50; Favourable below 0.30.
B4.reason: Pearson r = 0.72 with n = 68: level and variability move together, so one pooled z-score threshold treats high-variability countries differently.

findings.detail: The 1980s-to-1990s country means correlate at Pearson r = 0.92 (95% cluster-bootstrap interval 0.90 to 0.95) and Spearman rho = 0.96 (n = 63). The 1990s-to-2000–2005 pair is r = 0.95, Spearman rho = 0.94 (n = 67).

findings.title: Coverage and rate level are not meaningfully associated among countries with at least 10 years.
findings.detail: Across all 196 entities, years reported and country mean correlate at Pearson r = 0.23 and Spearman rho = 0.26. Among the 68 entities with at least 10 years, Pearson r = -0.05 and Spearman rho = 0.04.
findings.caveat: The full sample includes many entities with only three observations; the subset is the relevant comparison.

findings.title: Level and variability move together, which affects pooled anomaly screening.
findings.detail: Among the 68 entities with at least 10 observations, country mean and the SD of yearly rates correlate at Pearson r = 0.72 and Spearman rho = 0.77. Within-country standardisation would flag 124 changes versus 122 under the pooled rule; 154 of 2,457 rows would change status.
findings.caveat: The existing anomaly table is unchanged; this is a sensitivity note about the screening rule.

findings.title: The trend correlation depends on who is included.
findings.detail: Pooled Pearson r is -0.02 for all 2,843 records and 0.09 for 1950–2001 (2,216 records). Within the eight complete panels it is 0.19 (n = 448), their yearly average gives 0.72 (n = 56), and the 32 entities with at least 40 years give 0.11 (n = 1,637).
findings.caveat: A1–A2 mix changing country groups; A4 correlates a yearly average, not individual observations. These are descriptive associations only.
